# Synthetic pre-refactor replay and journal fixtures

## Baseline 536b42b5 and reduced v1 journal

The generator ran with the TrackmaniaRL checkout at commit
`536b42b56417ba9c84237d4555a6df73d00bf589`. It produced a distributed schema
2 checkpoint with two synthetic transitions and a sequence sampler, then
committed a third transition to the matching journal after the checkpoint. The
first journal row was pruned by the completed checkpoint; both receipts remain.

The journal file is **synthetic v1**, not an artifact emitted by a historical v1
release: after closing the baseline v2 journal the generator removed the three
v2 evaluation tables and set `schema_version` to `1`. It zlib-compressed the
result for storage. The checkpoint is the baseline's unmodified zstd-streamed
Torch checkpoint. There is no real game or training data in either fixture.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `checkpoint-v2-536b42b5.bin` | `467c5e6d8eb9cb611b3b227137f56d0b32b3673efc488b1aa6cd92aafb330152` |
| `journal-v1-536b42b5.bin` | `9d333006f46c79c4963e79955625e5e5ccd5844d7bef940ac9422c05029f61f0` |

To regenerate, use an isolated, clean checkout of exactly that commit, the
project's test dependencies, and one thread for Torch/OpenMP/MKL. Run the
generator from the newer checkout with `PYTHONPATH` set to the baseline root:

```text
python PATH_TO_THIS_GENERATOR NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
```

The output directory must not exist. The generator verifies the imported
package's Git HEAD, creates its own temporary run and never connects to a game.
It assigns a synthetic fixed run fingerprint and creates a random journal ID;
regenerated bytes and hashes therefore differ. The synthetic identity tests
format-level restore only. Normal exact resume still checks the actual run
fingerprint, which includes source-code identity and can reject a checkpoint
from a different revision even when its serialization format is readable.

## Historical v1.3.0 writer

The original TrackmaniaRL [v1.3.0 release](https://github.com/TrackmaniaRL/TrackmaniaRL/releases/tag/v1.3.0),
commit `eb803a2153d472ebb16cd7150201c82058dd804a`, generated these two fixtures
on 2026-11-12. They contain synthetic
transitions created for this test; they are not files from a historical training
run. Generation used Windows, Python 3.12.12, SQLite 3.50.4, NumPy 2.4.2 and
Torch 2.11.0+cu128 with one CPU thread; no GPU was used. The release's own
coordinator wrote the checkpoint and SQLite journal. The
generator verifies, using a read-only SQLite connection, that the journal is
schema v1 and contains exactly `chunks`, `actor_profiles`, `receipts`, and
`metadata`. No tables or metadata are rewritten. The journal is compressed
with zlib only after the coordinator closes it; checkpoint bytes are unchanged.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `checkpoint-v130-eb803a21.bin` | `26254cdb9ae47ad59f88d4695f74a2348e89d7e893849b6e9066f791b0afac2b` |
| `journal-v1-v130-eb803a21.bin` | `02fead608aa8fcc3d361d7c39ed2cae10c71c0b3c00823add9e7de436f2c9e40` |

To regenerate, use `generate_v130.py` with a clean, isolated checkout of exactly
`eb803a2153d472ebb16cd7150201c82058dd804a` on `PYTHONPATH`; run from that
checkout with the project test dependencies and `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`,
`MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`, and `NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1`.
Pass a new output directory that does not exist. The generator checks the
imported checkout's HEAD, uses a separate temporary run directory and calls the
coordinator in process without opening a game or listening port:

```text
python PATH_TO_GENERATE_V130_PY NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
```

As with the other pair, it fixes the synthetic run fingerprint and generates a
random journal ID, so regenerated hashes differ. The test restores the older
checkpoint and sampler, migrates the matching v1 journal, replays a later row,
checks the two original receipts and rejects a different fingerprint. It proves
this format-level scenario using the test suite's toy learner and pipeline; it
does not exercise a real trained policy or model parameters, exact resume across
different source fingerprints, or compatibility with every historical run.

## Historical v1.3.0 writer with a first-party learner

The additional `real` pair was generated on 2026-11-12 by the same unmodified
v1.3.0 release, commit `eb803a2153d472ebb16cd7150201c82058dd804a`. It uses
synthetic data and a small first-party `DiscreteValueLearner` with an MLP sensor
encoder, identity temporal core and scalar Q head. One synthetic update before
the coordinator's checkpoint makes Adam state nonempty. Two transitions precede
the checkpoint and one follows in the journal. The original coordinator writes
both artifacts, and the generator checks the v1 journal schema read-only before
zlib compression; it does not modify the journal. No game or port is used.

Generation used Windows, Python 3.12.12, SQLite 3.50.4, NumPy 2.4.2 and Torch
2.11.0+cu128 with CUDA hidden before importing Torch and one CPU thread. The
fixture contains no CUDA RNG state. The model is freshly initialized and is not
a trained policy from an actual run.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `checkpoint-real-v130-eb803a21.bin` | `daa2270faf240386dc2ed5dda14fa0abc820fbd1261f4607d960e7f68387cbd2` |
| `journal-real-v1-v130-eb803a21.bin` | `c337f2f258a9dc2a394f02af2f8d22eb4c450fdef591d40358d47879260eac4a` |

To regenerate, run `generate_real_v130.py` from a clean isolated checkout of
the exact release with that checkout on `PYTHONPATH`, an unused output path and
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`,
`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`, and `NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1` set before Python starts.
The generator verifies the imported package's Git HEAD, refuses visible CUDA,
and creates its intermediate run in a separate temporary directory. Random
journal identity and checkpoint serialization mean regenerated hashes differ.

The checkpoint records the actual fingerprint computed in that historical
environment. One test uses the low-level coordinator with that recorded value
explicitly supplied to examine the format: it verifies the complete learner
state, sampler, migration, receipts and replay recovery, then performs one CPU
update from the recovered synthetic replay. A second test uses the fingerprint
computed from the current configuration and source and verifies rejection
before mutating the learner or replay. The mismatch reflects the full
fingerprint inputs, not necessarily source changes alone. Supplying the old
identity in the format test does not demonstrate ordinary cross-version exact
resume or compatibility with other learner architectures and configurations.
